summary: Lexington County Bethlehem Steel tower on an 80-foot galvanized steel tower, one of two still standing in its original spot in the county; in poor condition when registered in 2013.

facts.design: Bethlehem Steel tower with a 7'x7' steel cab on an 80-foot galvanized steel tower
facts.agency: South Carolina Forestry Commission (believed to administer it, per the register)

events.note: The Forestry Commission closed its tower system on 1 October 1993; this tower's own build year is not given

evidence.supports: one of the original ~140 SCFC towers built mid-1930s to 1993
evidence.quote: This is one of the original ~140 fire towers built by the South Carolina Forestry Commission between the mid-1930s and the abandonment of the system in 1993.

evidence.supports: one of two still standing in original location in Lexington County
evidence.quote: This tower is one of two still standing in its original location in Lexington County.

evidence.supports: Bethlehem Steel tower, 7x7 steel cab, 80-foot galvanized steel tower
evidence.quote: The lookout is a Bethlehem Steel tower with a 7'-by-7' steel cab on top of an 80-foot galvanized steel tower.

evidence.supports: shed at base appears to house radio equipment; antennas on tower
evidence.quote: appears to house radio equipment and several antennas are mounted on the tower
believed to be South Carolina Forestry Commission
The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

evidence.supports: Gaston: three towers in Lexington County still owned by SCFC
evidence.quote: is one of three still owned by the SC Forestry Commission in Lexington county

notes_for_editor: Only the register and the SCFC history page were usable; no build year, operator or fire history for this tower turned up in two searches. The register's 'one of the original ~140' figure is not the same as a later SCFC social post that says 'more than 130'; that post was not fetched and is not cited. The register calls the tower in poor condition as of 2013; no newer condition report was found. Height 80 ft converted to 24.4 m, matching the record.
